body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. A 16-year-old boy was killed in an early-morning shooting at a large party in southwest Bakersfield, and a woman died after being struck by a police patrol vehicle on White Lane — two of the hardest stories we've had to write in a while, and both are below. Otherwise, expect a cool, clear Sunday: a high near 62, air quality sitting at a healthy 26, and no weather alerts anywhere in Kern County.

## The Kern Overnight

The night's most serious call came at 11:45 p.m., when officers and an ambulance were sent to the 4000 block of Rosedale Highway for a shooting with two victims. Units moved in on emergency traffic, and the suspect vehicle was described as a black four-door Mercedes. No further details were available by morning.

Gunfire reports kept dispatchers busy across the city. Callers in the 12200 block of Margalo Avenue reported three to four loud explosions and three gunshots at 7:53 p.m., followed by four shots and a vehicle driving east at 8:19 p.m. Three to four shots were reported near Del Pino and Belle Terrace at 8:27 p.m., and a possible shooting toward a person came in at 10:38 p.m. Just after midnight, two men were reported setting off fireworks at each other in the middle of a street.

A business in the 3700 block of Ming Avenue was robbed at 8:47 p.m. by a suspect reported to have a knife, who fled east in a gray van. At 4:16 a.m., a man walked into a store in the 300 block of South Martin Luther King Boulevard covered in blood and asking for help; officers responded to what was logged as a possible assault. Kern County Fire crews and an ambulance were sent to a structure fire at 2:05 a.m., and crews were called to the 12000 block of Lamberton Street in northwest Bakersfield at 5:49 a.m., where a woman was reported dead.

Weapons calls came in through the evening and early morning — a man with a firearm in a red pickup who left before officers arrived, a man in a gray sedan reportedly armed with two juveniles in the car near Geraldine Street and South Union Avenue, a caller who said his wife was being threatened by a woman with a gun, a resident reportedly telling another woman to shoot her, and a call at a Rio Morada apartment. Wrong-way drivers were reported twice: southbound in the northbound lanes at 2:24 a.m., and westbound in the eastbound lanes of Highway 58 at Fairfax Road at 3:59 a.m., where dispatch took multiple 911 calls.

## Today's weather

It's 57 degrees at Meadows Field this morning, and we're headed to a high near 62 with a low around 49 tonight — a genuinely pleasant fall Sunday, the kind that makes the valley feel like it's finally exhaling. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and no active fires reported. Air quality is 26, which registers as good, so it's a fine day to be outside, take the dog a little farther than usual, or get the yard work done before the light goes.

## Top stories

**Bakersfield Now reports a large police presence near Challenger Park in southwest Bakersfield.** Details were still limited as of this morning, and we'll pass along more as it becomes available. If you were in the area and saw something, it's worth keeping an eye on the outlet's updates through the day.

**According to 23ABC, a 16-year-old boy was killed in a shooting at a large party in southwest Bakersfield early Saturday.** Police responded around 3:35 a.m. to several reports of gunshots near South Half Moon Drive, where they found the teen suffering major injuries. He was taken to a hospital and pronounced dead, and police say they are still searching for possible suspects. Anyone with information is asked to call the Bakersfield Police Department at (661) 327-7111.

**KGET 17 reports that a woman died after being struck by a Bakersfield police patrol vehicle in the area of White Lane early Saturday.** Around 2:44 a.m., the officer behind the wheel had been dispatched to a call and was traveling eastbound when the woman walked out into the roadway in front of the patrol vehicle. Police say she entered the road from the south side and was not in a crosswalk, and she was pronounced dead at the scene. The department's Traffic Division is asking anyone with information to call 661-327-7111.

**23ABC tells us a Kern County nonprofit has been hosting meetings to walk Spanish-speaking voters through the propositions on their ballots ahead of the election.** Building Healthy Communities held one of those sessions Friday evening at Chepe's Mexican Restaurant in Arvin, part of a coalition effort that has also partnered with groups in McFarland. President Reyna Olaguez said turnout has been strong, especially among older Latina women who may not have voted before, and first-time voter Nancy Rodriguez said the meeting helped her understand a ballot that had felt overwhelming. With the election just days away, it's a reminder that plain-language help is reaching voters who want it.

**From KGET 17, a Southern California doctor has been sentenced to prison for a $45 million Medicare fraud scheme.** The case is a reminder of how much money moves through federal health programs and how aggressively prosecutors pursue those who skim from them — a story worth watching for anyone in Kern County who works in health care billing or compliance.

**KGET 17 also has its eye on the six races that could decide control of the Senate.** It's a national story, but a useful one to skim this morning if you want to understand what the final days of this election cycle are actually hinging on.

## Something good

Golden Empire Transit is offering free rides to veterans and active-duty military members throughout November. The promotion gives local service members and veterans no-cost access to public transit across Bakersfield and Kern County — a small, practical thank-you that can make a real difference for folks getting to appointments, work, or family. If you or someone you know qualifies, it's worth taking advantage of all month long.

## Coming up this week

It's a busy week at City Hall. The City Council meets twice on Wednesday, Nov. 4 — first at 3:30 p.m. for Meeting 330, then again at 5:15 p.m. for Meeting 515. Also Wednesday, the Police Civil Service Commission meets at 8:30 a.m. The Planning Commission follows on Thursday, Nov. 5, at 5:30 p.m. Agendas for each are posted ahead of time, and public comment is open at all of them.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate this month. Journey USA takes the stage Saturday, Nov. 7, alongside TEXAS TORNADO TRADITION the same day. Cults & Classics: Play Misty for Me screens Monday, Nov. 9, and NUTCRACKER! Magical Christmas Ballet arrives Friday, Nov. 13. The 20th Anniversary of the Bakersfield Country Music Awards lands Saturday, Nov. 15 — a good one to circle if you love local music. And if you're already thinking ahead, season passes for Cults & Classics 2026–2027 are on sale now.

Have a good Sunday, Bakersfield. Check on your neighbors, and we'll see you tomorrow.

top.title: Large police presence reported near Challenger Park in southwest Bakersfield
